newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by active bids/offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Supported by active bids/offers.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices stayed firm on Wednesday amid continued buying support from a local trading company, traders said.
A 380-cst cargo was traded at $97.00 per tonne for July 24-28, the same trading level on Tuesday, they said.
Interest was also seen in the 180-cst grade, with an offer at around $101.00 per tonne for a late July lifting cargo and a bid at $99.00 for early August loading, traders said.

The local trader has so far bought at least 160,000 tonnes of fuel oil for July and August loading and there were still market expectations that the trader would continue its spate of recent purchases.
"There is no sign he will stop buying soon," said one trader.
"But he cannot manipulate the fuel oil market like he did in the gas oil market because he is suffering now from plunging gas oil prices," said another trader.
The local trader was believed to have bought to cover its positions to supply term contracts, with some saying the cargoes are going to Indonesia.
Fuel oil swaps were steady to slightly lower, with July quoted at $98.50/$99.25 per tonne against Tuesday's $99.25/$100.00. August swaps were at $98.75/$99.50.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, sentiment remained strong due to tighter supplies in July, traders said.
Pertamina allocated just 2.3 million barrels of LSWR for July, with an additional 300,000 barrels, bringing the total July export volumes to 2.6 million barrels.
In June, Pertamina allocated 3.1 million barrels.
The reduced supplies from Indonesia was due to a shutdown of a 100,000 barrel-per-day crude unit at Cilicap refinery.
"The price should stay firmly above $16.00-per-barrel level," said one trader.
